news.title: AI今年主导IPO市场
news.snippet: [今年以来，人工智能（AI）在股权IPO市场表现突出，新股发行格局也呈现类似趋势。]
news.raw_snippet:
A similar pattern has emerged in this year’s equity initial public offering (IPO) market. AI and related infrastructure companies account for more than 80% of cumulative IPO value, driven in large part by huge offerings from SpaceX and Anthropic. More broadly, eight of the ten largest IPOs in 2026 are in the AI-related space when including industrial, energy, and utility companies tied to data center development. [...] # AI has dominated the IPO market this year

Markets & Economy

If one word captures artificial intelligence’s impact on the economy, it is “dominant”. In the first three quarters of this year, AI-related investment accounted for about two-thirds of GDP growth.1 More than 40% of investment-grade bond issuance so far this year has come from AI-focused companies – roughly double the share two years ago.2 [...] Meanwhile, AI-related IPOs have mostly fared poorly since trading in the secondary market. The table below shows returns for the thirteen AI-themed firms that raised at least $1 billion in their IPOs. Twelve are trading below their offering price, with an average return of -32%.

news.raw_snippet:
# Dunzo founder's AI startup M raises $9M to automate the home

What's the deal? M, the artificial intelligence startup founded by Dunzo co-founder Kabeer Biswas, has raised $9 million in a seed extension led by US venture firm RTP Global. RTP Global contributed $5 million, with existing investors adding the remaining $4 million, according to a November report by Moneycontrol. [...] The money trail: The round takes M's total funding to roughly $20 million. It follows an $11 million seed round in April 2026 backed by Peak XV Partners, Blume Ventures, and CRED.

What's the endgame? M is building an AI-powered household concierge that aims to automate the decisions and coordination involved in running a home. It is starting with kitchen management — meal planning, tracking grocery needs, and coordinating with domestic staff. [...] Read more: lapaasvoice.com

news.title: 企业家Abigail Horne称AI需保留“人的一层”
news.snippet: [Abigail Horne认为，AI系统应加入人类监督层，确保人与AI代理共同决策时的问责机制。]
news.raw_snippet:
– Accountability when people and AI agents make decisions together in the workplace  
– Using AI to direct donated goods to communities with the greatest need and to help workers arrange shift preferences  
– How founders seeking investment balance profit with ethical aims [...] SAN FRANCISCO, CA, UNITED STATES, November 27, 2026 /EINPresswire.com/ — Tomorrow, Today, the long-form interview series created and hosted by Shekhar Natarajan, has released a new episode featuring Abigail Horne, the British entrepreneur and co-founder of publishing company Authors & Co. The conversation focuses on trust in artificial intelligence (AI), the role of human values in automated decisions and what accountability looks like when people and AI systems work together. [...] Throughout the conversation, Horne presses on what happens when powerful AI tools operate without safeguards built around human values. She raises the growing use of humanoid robots in homes and caregiving, asks how a company’s values can be enforced when machines make decisions, and questions how a founder who criticizes the pursuit of profit approaches investors. “It is dangerous without this sort of human layer that you are trying to put in,” Horne said.
